back: A coordinating conjunction used to connect words, phrases, or clauses that are considered together or added to one another. The biology student needed safety goggles and a lab apron before beginning the specimen dissection.
extra: Adapted from Wiktionary coordinating conjunction gloss (expressing two elements taken together); distinguishes additive coordination from contrastive conjunctions.

front: The chemistry teacher stored the clean glass beakers {{c1::in}} the locked supply cabinet.
extra: The chemistry teacher stored the clean glass beakers in the locked supply cabinet.

back: A possessive determiner indicating that an object, idea, or attribute belongs to a previously mentioned female individual. Sophia brought her graphing calculator to advanced algebra so she could plot quadratic equations without delay.
extra: Grounded in Wiktionary possessive sense (Belonging to her); focused on student-friendly possessive determiner role rather than objective pronoun usage.

front: Before the interscholastic debate round commenced, each team {{c1::had}} fifteen minutes to organize their rebuttal evidence.
extra: Before the interscholastic debate round commenced, each team had fifteen minutes to organize their rebuttal evidence.

back: An adverb expressing denial, refusal, or the grammatical negation of a word, phrase, or clause. The high school librarian reminded the class that personal food and open beverage containers were not permitted near the reference computers.
extra: Grounded in WordNet not.r.01 (negation of a word or group of words); highlights formal syntactic negation in academic writing.

front: The administration rescheduled the regional track meet, {{c1::for}} severe convective storms were predicted across the county.
extra: The administration rescheduled the regional track meet, for severe convective storms were predicted across the county.

back: A preposition identifying a specific point, position, or general vicinity in space or physical location. The student council representatives assembled at the media center entrance promptly after the final afternoon bell.
extra: Selected Wiktionary spatial sense (In, near, or in the general vicinity of a particular place) rather than WordNet astatine.n.01.

front: Thorough textual evidence {{c1::is}} mandatory when defending a literary argument in tenth-grade English.
extra: Thorough textual evidence is mandatory when defending a literary argument in tenth-grade English.

back: Existing in an active, functioning, operational, or energized state. Before leaving the chemistry laboratory workstation, each pair verified that no electrical burners remained on.
extra: Selected WordNet on.a.01 (in operation or operational) and Wiktionary functional state sense rather than spatial preposition to target academic vocabulary nuances.

front: When the lab partners observed the chemical precipitate, {{c1::they}} recorded the exact color transition in their lab journals.
extra: When the lab partners observed the chemical precipitate, they recorded the exact color transition in their lab journals.

back: Stated, declared, or expressed thoughts in spoken or written language. During the Socratic discussion, Jordan said that the author's recurring ocean motif symbolized personal isolation.
extra: Grounded in WordNet state.v.01 (express in words); notes the distinction from Wiktionary legalistic adjective sense (aforesaid).

front: Elena set her primary source documents {{c1::by}} the laptop so she could cross-reference citations efficiently.
extra: Elena set her primary source documents by the laptop so she could cross-reference citations efficiently.

back: A subordinating conjunction introducing a hypothetical condition, presupposition, or required circumstance. An essay receives an exemplary score on the analytical rubric if every central claim is corroborated by convincing textual evidence.
extra: Grounded in Wiktionary conditional sense (Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that); reinforces conditional sentence structures.

front: The testing supervisor confirmed that {{c1::no}} unauthorized electronic devices were permitted on desks during the exam.
extra: The testing supervisor confirmed that no unauthorized electronic devices were permitted on desks during the exam.
